AL.name: Alabama
AL.statute: Ala. Code § 16-28A-1 (teachers may use corporal punishment 'as may be prescribed by the local board'; immunity if policy followed)
AL.notes: No statutory limits: no consent, disability, witness, instrument or record rules. Third-highest per-capita use (5.4 per 1,000 in 2021-22; 4,083 students; 4,352 in 2023-24, the only large-use state that rose). No ban bill found in 2023 or 2026; the 2024 and 2025 sessions could not be searched (site blocks automation).

AR.name: Arkansas
limits: No corporal punishment on a child who is intellectually disabled, non-ambulatory, non-verbal, or autistic (Act 557 of 2019, SB 381)
Only for cause, reasonable, after warning, by a teacher or administrator, in the presence of an administrator or designee (§ 6-18-503(b)); district must authorize it in its written discipline policy

bills.summary: Expanded staff authority to use 'reasonable and appropriate physical force'; not a ban

AR.notes: Second-highest per-capita use (6.3 per 1,000 in 2021-22; 3,165 students). A 2025 thesis reportedly counts 171 districts (72 percent) allowing and 51 banning. The disability ban is Act 557 of 2019, not 'Act 1249 of 2021' as some lists say. No ban bill found 2025-26 (Arkansans Against School Paddling tracker).

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.statute: A.R.S. § 15-843(B)(2) (boards prescribe 'procedures for using corporal punishment if allowed by the governing board')

bills.summary: Prohibit corporal punishment by any district or charter employee; second read Feb 4, 2026, no further action
Prohibit corporal punishment; died without a hearing
Prohibit corporal punishment; died without a hearing
Prohibit corporal punishment; died without a hearing

AZ.notes: Districts set their own rules; 72 students in 2021-22, 202 in 2023-24. A ban bill has been filed every year since 2023 and never received a hearing.

CO.name: Colorado
CO.notes: Signed and effective April 20, 2023; covers public schools including charters and licensed child care, not private schools. Before the law, 154 of 178 districts already prohibited it. House 48-16, Senate 32-0.

FL.name: Florida
FL.statute: Fla. Stat. § 1003.32(1)(k) (teacher authority per board policy) and § 1002.20(4)(c) (as amended by CS/HB 1255, 2025, ch. 2025-110)
limits: Since July 1, 2025 a board that authorizes it must require parental consent, for the school year or before each instance (the statute says 'consent,' not 'written consent'); the board must review the policy at a public meeting every three years or the authorization expires; charters must comply (§ 1002.33(16)(b)17)
Principal approval in principle and principal guidelines; another adult present and informed of the reason; written explanation to the parent on request (§ 1003.32(1)(k))
No disability ban

bills.sponsor: Rep. Johanna López (D), Sen. Mack Bernard (D)
bills.summary: Full ban for district employees; died in committee March 13, 2026

bills.sponsor: Reps. Dana Trabulsy and Chase Tramont (R)
bills.summary: Omnibus education bill adding the parental-consent requirement; final votes 100-0 and 30-0; signed May 30, 2025

bills.sponsor: Reps. Waldron, Beltran, Garcia, Gottlieb, Stark; Sen. Thompson
bills.summary: Remove teacher authority, require notification, ban for specified students; favorable in subcommittee, died March 8, 2024

FL.notes: 17 of 67 districts reported 516 instances in 2023-24 (Suwannee 74, Holmes 65, Calhoun 59, Columbia 50, Wakulla 45, Washington 43); 647 students in the 2021-22 federal count. Districts that still permit it are coded consent_required. The consent law came from a four-year University of Florida student campaign after a disability-only ban was blocked. Hendry County banned it in 2021 after a principal was filmed paddling a six-year-old.

GA.name: Georgia
limits: Not excessive or unduly severe; not a first-line punishment unless the pupil was warned; administered in the presence of a principal, assistant principal or designee informed beforehand in the pupil's presence; written explanation to the parent on request

No corporal punishment on a child whose parent filed, on the day of enrollment, a Georgia-licensed physician's statement that it would be detrimental to the child's mental or emotional stability (§ 20-2-731)

bills.sponsor: Reps. Debra Bazemore, James Beverly, Sam Park, Carolyn Hugley (D)
bills.summary: Prohibit corporal punishment in any public school; died after second reading

GA.notes: Near-dormant: a May 2026 Savannah Morning News review identified six districts with permitting policies (Wilcox, Laurens, Coffee, Tattnall, Appling, Heard; reported). 1,547 students in 2021-22; 1,127 in 2023-24. No ban bill in 2025-26.

IA.name: Iowa
IA.notes: Banned in both public and private schools

ID.name: Idaho
ID.notes: Signed April 3, 2023, effective July 1, 2023. Bundled with restraint and seclusion limits; private schools removed by Senate amendment. House 45-22, Senate 21-12.

IL.name: Illinois
IL.notes: Public-school ban dates to the mid-1990s (reported). HB 4175 (Rep. Margaret Croke) extended it to nonpublic schools; signed August 9, 2024, effective January 1, 2025.

IN.name: Indiana
IN.statute: No corporal punishment statute; IC 20-33-8-8(b) (school personnel 'stand in the relation of parents' and may take 'any disciplinary action necessary')

bills.summary: Ban corporal punishment in public, charter and state-accredited nonpublic schools; no hearing

IN.notes: No law explicitly bans or allows it; 8 students reported in 2021-22, 16 in 2017-18. SB 531's inclusion of nonpublic schools confirms no existing private-school ban.

KS.name: Kansas
KS.statute: No school corporal punishment statute; only K.S.A. 21-5602 (criminal child abuse, 'cruel and inhuman corporal punishment')
KS.notes: The state education department's general counsel (May 2025): 'there are no state laws that address corporal punishment' for K-12. The Kansas Association of School Boards model policy JDA says corporal punishment 'shall not be permitted,' adopted by many districts. Zero students reported in 2017-18, 2020-21 and 2021-22. No bill 2023-26. Kept as 'legal' because nothing prohibits it; effectively unused.

KY.name: Kentucky
limits: Under 704 KAR 7:170 (effective Aug 30, 2022) a district that permits it must obtain annual written and per-instance verbal parental consent, use a same-gender certified witness, no instruments, provide counseling by the next school day, and may not use it on students with IEPs or 504 plans, homeless or foster youth

bills.summary: Ban corporal punishment in schools; passed House 65-17, died in Senate Education
Ban corporal punishment in schools; died in committee

KY.notes: All 171 districts had prohibiting policies by November 2, 2023; zero incidents in 2023-24 (5 in 2022-23, 142 in 2019-20, about 1,100 in 2011-12). The statute still permits it, and advocates want a ban in law because policies can be reversed.

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.statute: La. R.S. 17:416.1(B) (public; Acts 2017 No. 266, 2023 No. 268, 2024 No. 780) and 17:416.22 (state-funded nonpublic schools)
limits: Prohibited in any public school unless the parent gives written consent for that school year on a form created by the state Department of Education (Act 268 of 2023, HB 242, effective August 1, 2023)
No corporal punishment on a student with an exceptionality (other than gifted) or an Individual Accommodation Plan (Act 266 of 2017)
Taping a student's mouth or otherwise restricting the airway is prohibited regardless of consent (Act 780 of 2024, HB 107)
The same rules apply to any nonpublic school that receives state funds (R.S. 17:416.22)

bills.summary: Written annual parental opt-in on a state form; House 74-21, Senate 37-1, signed June 9, 2023
Ban on mouth-taping and airway restriction regardless of consent; law without signature June 25, 2024
Opt-in consent; passed the House, died at sine die (the Global Initiative wrongly reports it as passed)
Full ban; failed the House 48-49

LA.notes: Louisiana is the clearest opt-in state: since August 2023 a school may not paddle without the parent's signed annual consent on the state form. A 2022 survey found 27 systems prohibiting and 19 allowing of 46 responding. 264 students in 2021-22; 65 in 2023-24. No bill in 2025 or 2026.

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.notes: Second state to ban (104 years after NJ)

MD.name: Maryland
MD.notes: Nonpublic-school ban effective July 1, 2023, through the State Board's certificate of approval; schools operated by a bona fide church organization are exempt from the certificate requirement.

MO.name: Missouri
limits: No pupil may be subject to corporal punishment without the parent being notified and providing written permission (opt-in, effective August 28, 2022)
Spanking must be administered by certificated personnel in the presence of a district-employee witness to be exempt from the abuse definition (160.261.10)
Each board's written discipline policy must state its determination on corporal punishment

bills.summary: Require every district policy to prohibit corporal punishment; referred May 15, 2026, no hearing
Require district policies to prohibit corporal punishment; no hearing
Require district policies to prohibit corporal punishment; no hearing
Require district policies to prohibit corporal punishment; no hearing

MO.notes: At least 123 districts authorized corporal punishment for 2022-23 (Columbia Missourian, April 2023). Cassville R-IV reinstated opt-in paddling in August 2022. 1,133 students in 2021-22; 1,002 in 2023-24. Ban bills have never received a hearing.

MS.name: Mississippi
MS.statute: Miss. Code Ann. § 37-11-57 (as amended by HB 1182, 2019, Laws 2019 ch. 354)
limits: No corporal punishment on any student with a disability (IEP or 504 plan), with no immunity for violations (effective July 1, 2019). No consent, witness, instrument or record requirements in statute

bills.summary: Full ban; died in committee Feb 3, 2026
Parental opt-in and annual notice; died in committee Feb 3, 2026
Full ban; died in committee Feb 3, 2026
All died in committee without a hearing
All died in committee
All died in committee

MS.notes: Highest per-capita use in the nation: 3,678 students in 2021-22 (8.3 per 1,000), 20,309 in 2017-18. Students with disabilities struck fell from 3,304 to 30 after the 2019 law, though Mississippi Today reported 211 paddlings of students with disabilities after the ban. Twelve bills in four sessions, three per year from the same three sponsors (a Democratic full ban in each chamber and a Republican opt-in), have all died in committee without a hearing. February 2025: an East Jasper third-grader's arm was broken during a paddling the mother had approved; no action found.

NC.name: North Carolina
limits: Local board decides; witness required; written parental notice; records; annual report to State Board by race, sex and disability; written parental opt-out offered at enrollment (an opted-out student may be suspended for offenses that otherwise would not require it)

bills.sponsor: Reps. Maria Cervania and Marcia Morey (D)
bills.summary: Prohibit corporal punishment in schools; in House Rules since April 14, 2025

bills.sponsor: Sen. Gladys Robinson (D) with Sen. Kevin Corbin (R) among sponsors
bills.summary: Prohibit corporal punishment in schools; in Senate Rules since March 26, 2025

NC.notes: All 115 districts prohibited it by October 2, 2018 (Robeson County April 2018, Graham County October 2, 2018) after two decades of advocacy by NC Child. 57 students reported in 2017-18; none since. A 2019 bipartisan ban bill cleared House Education and stalled.

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.notes: No express prohibition but not practiced

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.notes: First state to ban. Banned in both public and private schools

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.notes: Signed April 6, 2011 by Gov. Susana Martinez (R); effective June 17, 2011 (computed). House 36-31, Senate 22-17. Only 36 of 89 districts still permitted it at passage.

NY.name: New York
NY.notes: Public-school ban by regulation since 1985; the 2023 law, signed October 25, 2023, directs the Commissioner to prohibit corporal punishment in any school in the state, public or private.

OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.statute: 70 O.S. § 24-100.4(C) (teacher has a parent's right to discipline 'according to district policies'; formerly § 6-114); 21 O.S. § 844 ('spanking, switching or paddling'); 70 O.S. § 13-116 (disability ban, SB 364, 2025)
limits: No corporal punishment on any student identified with a disability under IDEA (SB 364, Laws 2025 ch. 99; law without the governor's signature May 8, 2025; effective about August 28, 2025 by constitutional default since the emergency clause failed)
70 O.S. § 24-100.4(D): the State Board may not proscribe corporal punishment except for IEP students, so Kentucky's regulatory route is closed by statute in Oklahoma
No statewide consent, witness, instrument or record rules

bills.sponsor: Sen. Dave Rader and Rep. Anthony Moore (R)
bills.summary: Ban corporal punishment for any student with an IDEA disability; Senate 31-16, House 63-25; became law without Gov. Stitt's signature
Reporting requirement; stalled
Disability ban; failed 45-43 March 14, 2023, passed 84-8 on reconsideration March 20, passed both chambers in different forms, died

OK.notes: 1,458 students in 2021-22 (991 in 2023-24); fourth-highest rate. American Indian/Alaska Native students were 24 percent of those struck in 2017-18. Bills carried by Republicans without an outside coalition. Note the statutory bar on State Board rulemaking: the Kentucky regulation route is unavailable here without a statute change.

SC.name: South Carolina
SC.notes: Unchanged since 1973: each district's governing body 'may provide corporal punishment for any pupil that it deems just and proper.' No statutory limits and no State Board regulation. 85 students in 2021-22, 23 in 2017-18. No bill on school corporal punishment filed in the 2023-24 or 2025-26 sessions. District-by-district status unverified; an Island Packet explainer of September 18, 2025 likely has a tally.

TN.name: Tennessee
limits: Before corporal punishment the educator must document having addressed the behavior, provided consequences, consulted the parent, and considered whether to evaluate the student for a disability (Public Chapter 275, effective April 28, 2023)

No corporal punishment on a student with a disability unless district policy permits it and the parent gives written permission specifying type and circumstances, with notice each time (HB 2330, 2018)
Each local board adopts rules to implement and control any form of corporal punishment (§ 49-6-4104)

bills.sponsor: Sen. Bill Powers (R), Rep. John Stevens (R); co-primes Sens. Akbari, Campbell
bills.summary: Documentation prerequisites before corporal punishment; Senate 32-0, House 90-0, signed April 28, 2023

bills.sponsor: Sen. Heidi Campbell (D), Rep. Jason Powell (D)
bills.summary: Full ban removing statutory authorization; SB 1788 failed for lack of a second in Senate Education March 13, 2024; HB 1965 taken off notice

TN.notes: 1,031 students in 2021-22; 616 in 2023-24 (down 40 percent, after the 2023 documentation law). No bill in the 2025-26 session by caption search. Jackson County: a teacher and assistant principal were indicted in November 2023 after two paddlings injured a student; outcome not found.

TX.name: Texas
limits: If the student code of conduct permits it, a district educator may use corporal punishment unless the parent has provided a signed written statement prohibiting it, renewed each school year (opt-out)
Tex. Educ. Code § 22.0512 bars districts from disciplining an employee for force justified under Penal Code § 9.62

bills.summary: Prohibit corporal punishment (new § 37.901); died in Public Education without a hearing
Affirmative parental consent before corporal punishment; died without a hearing
Reporting and opt-out notice; died without a hearing
Ban corporal punishment in public schools; committee 5-2, failed on second reading April 26, 2023 (reported 58-86); Allen has filed it every session for 18 years

TX.notes: Largest absolute use: 7,324 students in 2021-22 and 5,359 in 2023-24; 13,892 in 2017-18. IDRA counted 468 districts with corporal punishment policies in 2017-18. Overton ISD, 2023: a principal's assault charge for a bruising paddling was dismissed because district policy was followed and the mother consented. Millsap ISD, 2025: indictments over staff striking an autistic student (abuse, not sanctioned paddling).

WY.name: Wyoming
WY.statute: W.S. § 21-4-308(b) (immunity for reasonable corporal discipline authorized by board policy)

bills.summary: Repeal immunity for corporal discipline; Senate 26-5, House Committee of the Whole failed 12-47 on February 14, 2023
Require district discipline policies, parental notice and reporting; repeal the corporal-discipline immunity; failed introduction 38-24 (two-thirds needed) February 9, 2026

WY.notes: The statute grants immunity rather than authorizing the practice. Press in 2022-23 reported one to three of 48 districts still had it in policy (Niobrara County SD #1 named) and no incidents reported federally since 2012; Laramie County SD 1 reaffirmed its prohibition in October 2025. Advocate: principal Jeff Jones.
